clue.text: Boy with an inner compulsion to become a doctor

indicators.note: the boy is said to have something inside him, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
an urge is a compulsion

explanation.surface: A lad driven from within to qualify in medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, a kind of physician.

clue.text: Be in a state of suppressed anger about trainee being faster

indicators.note: the anger word goes round the learner, enclosing it

parts.words: Be in a state of suppressed anger
parts.note: to simmer is to seethe quietly
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Someone fuming quietly because a trainee works more quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' is not 'quicker' but one who fasts, a dieter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dieting to lose weight goes without food, so is one who fasts.

clue.text: Following some who declare sultan the absolute ruler

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Supporters who proclaim the sultan an autocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absolute ruler' is surface padding for the sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: Resultant means coming as a consequence, following on from something.

clue.text: Shortly the editor will receive people — so correct!

indicators.note: the editor takes in the people, holding them inside

parts.note: ED is the abbreviated form of editor
men are people

explanation.surface: Soon the editor takes on staff to fix the text.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to amend it, removing errors.

clue.text: Unfamiliar bazaar game

parts.note: something new is unfamiliar
a bazaar is a market

explanation.surface: A strange pastime played at an oriental market.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is also the English horse-racing town, but here it is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game in which players stake on cards laid out, also called Michigan.

clue.text: Going after tea to make notes

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
to sing is to produce musical notes with the voice

explanation.surface: Leaving after a cup of tea to go and write things down.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing something is pursuing it, running behind it to catch it.

clue.text: Scots cannot unearth a tropical plant

definitions.meaning: a lily-like flowering plant of warm regions

explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect 'can't' becomes canna, and the canna lily is a tropical ornamental flower.

clue.text: A safe haven can make a change — or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters go in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sheltered harbour can bring about a transformation, or not.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a sheltered place where ships can moor in safety.

clue.text: Angry robber losing his head

indicators.note: the robber loses his first letter

parts.note: a pirate is a robber at sea

explanation.surface: A furious thief on the point of being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' drops the P of PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious, very cross.

clue.text: Fish put on shore from deck

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
to land a catch or a boat is to bring it ashore

explanation.surface: A fish brought ashore off a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' is the verb meaning adorn, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To garland is to adorn with wreaths of flowers, to festoon.

clue.text: Question the children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a point under discussion
... is a formal word for offspring, as in 'died without ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A disputed point is an issue, and a family's descendants are its issue in legal language.

clue.text: Placed by the bird table?

parts.note: read as furniture named after part of a bird, a seat that one would put beside a table

explanation.surface: Something set out next to a garden feeder for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A bird table is where garden birds are fed; here it is split as a bird's limb plus a seat set at a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-backed armchair with side pieces projecting forward is named for those flaps, like a bird's limbs.

clue.text: Made moral version of this play

indicators.note: a new version of the words is a rearranged form of their letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drama rewritten to carry an improving lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage piece with stock heroes and villains.

clue.text: Love having money and time for musical entertainment

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
P stands for penny or pence
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Romance, cash and leisure all come together at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged drama set to music and sung throughout.

clue.text: Cook needs the right sort of oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven

explanation.surface: A chef demands the proper kind of oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a traditional English building for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to bake meat in dry heat, a way of preparing food.

clue.text: Brown is interrupting the story to tease

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: the word is breaks into the story, sitting inside it

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone brown interrupts a narrative just to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something kept just out of reach.

clue.text: Snatched the book

definitions.meaning: seized and carried off by force for ransom
the title of Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel

explanation.definitionFit: Abducted means taken away by force, and Stevenson's 1886 novel of David Balfour bears the same title.

clue.text: Many churchmen are men with businesses to run

parts.note: DI is 501 in Roman numerals, a large number
rectors are parish clergy

explanation.surface: Plenty of clergy turn out to be company managers.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors are those on a company's board who manage its affairs.

clue.text: Place, or it could be, in China

indicators.note: the words could become something else when their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere, or so it might be, in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link; 'China' is capitalised to suggest the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine ceramic ware, what we call china.

clue.text: Seeing Edward turn on a hill, one may well blow up!

indicators.note: to turn the name round is to read it backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Watching Edward wheel round on a hilltop, someone fears an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is a device that sets off an explosive charge.

clue.text: There is just no expression to describe this

definitions.text: There is just no expression to describe this

parts.words: There is just no expression to describe this
parts.note: seems to say the thing is indescribable, but means a face showing no expression at all

explanation.surface: Something words simply cannot capture.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker face showing no emotion, used especially of dry humour delivered impassively.

clue.text: The retreat of a great high-flier

definitions.text: The retreat of a great high-flier

parts.words: The retreat of a great high-flier
parts.note: a high-flier sounds like an ambitious person, but it is a large bird of prey and its lofty home

explanation.surface: Where a top achiever goes to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built on a crag or treetop is known by this name.

clue.text: The noble lady who got cross at every halt

definitions.text: The noble lady who got cross at every halt

parts.words: The noble lady who got cross at every halt
parts.note: got cross seems to mean became angry, but stone crosses were raised where her funeral procession stopped

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who lost her temper every time things stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward I set up memorial crosses at each overnight stop of his queen's funeral cortege from Lincoln to London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward I's queen, of Castile, is commemorated by crosses marking her funeral route.

clue.text: The main distributor of vital supplies

definitions.text: The main distributor of vital supplies

parts.words: The main distributor of vital supplies
parts.note: sounds like a wholesaler, but the vital supply is blood and the main channel is the largest artery

explanation.surface: A firm that carries the chief stock of essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest artery carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the whole body.

clue.text: Cut made by the sound builder

indicators.note: sound signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: a raiser is one who raises, puts up a building

explanation.surface: An injury caused by a reliable construction worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like the adjective meaning reliable but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladed instrument for shaving is what makes such a cut.

clue.text: Putting a member into care is dreadful — an outrage

indicators.note: the limb is put inside the scrambled letters
dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Admitting someone to a care home is called shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges CARE IS to SACRIE, and 'into' puts LEG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is violation of something sacred, a profane affront.

clue.text: Reserved about a pound, though that's easily split

indicators.note: the reserved word goes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: shy means reserved
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A timid person handed a pound, though that is soon divided.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaly rock is like shale, which splits readily into thin layers.

clue.text: Home help brought up in the country

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up reads it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic servant raised in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses AID to give DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country of south Asia.

clue.text: It requires pluck to play like this!

definitions.text: It requires pluck to play like this!

parts.words: It requires pluck to play like this!
parts.note: pluck seems to mean courage, but it is the plucking of strings with the fingers

explanation.surface: Performing in this manner takes nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling string players to pluck rather than bow.

clue.text: Pulled out looking harrowed

definitions.meaning: extracted, as a tooth or a sword
haggard and strained in the face

explanation.definitionFit: Something extracted has been drawn, and a tired, tense face is described as drawn.

clue.text: Care for miniature railway in the garden?

parts.note: to nurse is to tend or look after
RY is a short form of railway, the word made miniature

explanation.surface: Looking after a toy train set laid out in the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miniature' signals the abbreviated form of railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young plants are raised for sale, a garden of seedlings.

clue.text: A composer may break down in tears

indicators.note: breaking down the words lets their letters be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A songwriter could collapse weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stainer wrote The Crucifixion, an oratorio still sung in English churches.
